title: The Heart
subtitle: A pump about the size of your fist
intro: Point at any part of the heart to see what it does, or start the tour to follow one journey of blood around the body.

structures.name: Superior vena cava
structures.summary: The large vein that brings oxygen-poor blood back from the head, neck and arms to the right atrium.
structures.fact: A matching vein, the inferior vena cava, does the same job for the lower body.

structures.name: Right atrium
structures.summary: The upper right chamber. It receives oxygen-poor blood from the body and passes it down to the right ventricle.
structures.fact: A small cluster of cells in its wall, the sinoatrial node, sets the rhythm of every heartbeat.

structures.name: Right ventricle
structures.summary: The lower right chamber. It pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs through the pulmonary trunk.
structures.fact: It only has to reach the nearby lungs, so its wall is thinner than the left ventricle's.

structures.name: Pulmonary trunk
structures.summary: The large artery leaving the right ventricle. It divides into the left and right pulmonary arteries.

structures.name: Pulmonary arteries
structures.summary: They carry oxygen-poor blood from the heart to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen.
structures.fact: Unusually for arteries, they carry blood that is low in oxygen.

structures.name: Pulmonary veins
structures.summary: They bring freshly oxygenated blood from the lungs back to the left atrium.
structures.fact: Unusually for veins, they carry blood that is rich in oxygen.

structures.name: Left atrium
structures.summary: The upper left chamber. It collects oxygen-rich blood from the lungs and passes it down to the left ventricle.

structures.name: Left ventricle
structures.summary: The lower left chamber and the strongest part of the heart. It pumps oxygen-rich blood out to the whole body.
structures.fact: Its muscular wall is much thicker than the right ventricle's, because it must push blood all the way round the body.

structures.name: Aorta
structures.summary: The body's main artery. Oxygen-rich blood leaves the left ventricle through it and is carried on to every organ.
structures.fact: The coronary arteries, which feed the heart muscle itself, branch off close to its base.

tour.caption: Oxygen-poor blood comes back from the head, neck and arms through the superior vena cava.
It arrives in the right atrium, the first chamber of the heart.
The right ventricle squeezes it on towards the lungs.
The pulmonary trunk splits into two pulmonary arteries, one for each lung, where the blood picks up oxygen.
Freshly oxygenated blood returns from the lungs through the pulmonary veins.
It collects in the left atrium.
The left ventricle, the strongest chamber, pushes it out.
The blood leaves through the aorta and is carried to every part of the body. Then the journey starts again.
